learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the origin of life, Darwin's theory of natural selection, and how species change and adapt over millions of years!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Life started from non-living organic molecules in the Earth's primitive oceans. The famous Miller-Urey experiment proved this by creating amino acids in a lab using sparks (lightning) and ancient gases!

Fossils show how life changed over time. Homologous organs (like a human arm and a whale flipper) have the same structure but different functions, proving a shared ancestor. Analogous organs (like bird and butterfly wings) have different structures but the same function.
Nature selects the fittest! Organisms that are better adapted to their environment survive longer and leave more offspring. Over time, these advantageous traits become common in the population.

In a stable, non-evolving population, allele frequencies remain constant from generation to generation. The mathematical equation $p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$ helps scientists detect if evolution is currently happening.

We didn't evolve from modern monkeys; we share a common ancestor. The journey goes from Dryopithecus (ape-like) to Australopithecus (first to stand upright), Homo habilis (tool maker), Homo erectus (used fire), and finally to Homo sapiens (modern humans).

fun_activity.title: 🦋 The Peppered Moth Simulation
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine a forest of white birch trees. White moths blend in and survive, while black moths get eaten. Now imagine pollution turns the trees black. Suddenly, the black moths blend in and survive, and white moths get eaten! This actually happened during the Industrial Revolution.

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish clearly between Divergent evolution (homologous organs) and Convergent evolution (analogous organs). This is a highly tested topic.
📌 Know the factors that can disrupt Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium: Gene migration, Genetic drift, Mutation, Genetic recombination, and Natural selection.
📌 Be able to draw the graphs showing the three types of natural selection: Stabilizing, Directional, and Disruptive.
quick_recap: ⭐ Evolution is not a directed process; it is a stochastic (chance) process based on random mutations and natural selection.
⭐ Birds are actually the modern descendants of a group of theropod dinosaurs!
⭐ Genetic drift (random changes in gene frequency) is most prominent in very small populations.
